results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 68 aligned units' one-phrase summaries match the controlling ideas of their spec paragraphs in spec order (p01-p68, including the neutrality section opening with p17-p18); the five intro callouts match no spec paragraph and carry the thesis statement and roadmap callouts the spec places there.

The outliner marked three units as two-idea. Architecture ¶8 (p26): the model-output point is subordinate ('That record matters more as leads carry model outputs'), one idea about recording exports. Architecture ¶10 (p28): opened by one controlling sentence, 'Two architectural consequences follow; both are my inference from the published designs', which the spec's p28 controlling idea declares as one unit. Architecture ¶11 (p29): the OAuth baseline elaborates the third rule ('integrations are principals'), so it serves the three-rules idea. None needs two controlling ideas against its spec entry.

Every unit ties to S1-S4: concepts and worked-example Golf units to S1, workspace pieces/inventory/team to S2, partner API, trade-offs rule and agents to S3, neutrality, Keybridge boundary and group-exit separability to S4; failure modes, CA view and questions each map to one claim; conclusion performs the part's closing.

Tables 1-5 are each followed by a caption that states what they show and a paragraph drawing the consequence (p12, p35/p36, p39, p48, p52); Figures 1-5 are explained in their units (p16, p19-p20, p23, p39, p42-p43); quotations (P2B Arts. 7 and 9, Bundeskartellamt, Rightmove, Vinted, productscape) are each followed by the point they make. The renewal figures in p41 are covered under flow_is_followable.

Every declared transition_in, section and paragraph level, is expressed at its boundary: e.g. p02 contrast ('treated every seller the same way, but professionals supply most'), section openings 'Ingrid's first question' / 'The second question' / 'The third of Ingrid's questions', p33 contrast ('Whatever happens to the regulation'), p36 contrast ('The controls cost something'), trade-offs elaboration ('Keybridge is one of three ways'), verticals elaboration ('Which option fits also depends on the vertical'), failure-modes contrast ('The design fails in practice'), CA view cause_effect ('Preventing these failures'), p64 time ('will soon ... from 2025-2026'), questions sequence, conclusion summary. Whether the verticals bridge is delivered by the section is a flow finding, recorded there.

results.quote: from outcomes rather than exposure to the lead from their side
results.finding: The roadmap compresses section topics into phrases that do not parse until the sections arrive. Reader B misparsed 'exposure to the lead' as one phrase and re-read; reader A found 'building, integrating or owning' cryptic until the Trade-offs section names the three options. Same passage (the roadmap paragraph), same problem: over-compressed section labels. The spec's order is fine; plainer labels (e.g. 'whether to build tools, integrate partners through APIs or own pro software') fix it.

The introduction opens on an intriguing example (private seller vs. a dealer who lives in the marketplace), bridges to the reconciliation test and states the thesis in KEY POINTS; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic, and does not end on a restated thesis; the 90-second and 10-second targets it cites come from publication-pipeline as the spec's p67 evidence requires, serving the hand-off rather than holding body evidence.

p66 states what no section states alone (Part III is one chain from forms and feeds to the professional who checks it); p67 says why it matters (discovery can treat indices and alerts as read models, or inherits the ghost, the duplicate or the disputed count).

p66 returns to the hook ('it ends where this chapter began: with professionals who judge the marketplace by whether its numbers agree with their own'), the scene's two arguments (Ruhrblick's withdrawn downgrade, Claire's question) and the part's 'one chain, not five features'.

The cold reader predicted all ten sections in the spec's order (two arguments; what professionals need incl. outcomes over exposure and the lead from their side; workspace architecture; neutrality with the four controls and P2B; worked example settling both; build/integrate/own; verticals; failure modes; CA view; questions), the evidence (company filings and documentation, EU P2B law, fictional Veldmark) and a declarative practitioner tone, matching AC-2's expected answer.

The cold reader resolved both cases as expected: reconciled per channel into one ledger of 19 unique buyers, exported every channel through the Lead API and webhooks with stable IDs and deduplication keys, raw and deduplicated counts side by side, statistics/ledger/delivery from one event stream, opt-in VIN sale matching; refused the cross-portal data even anonymized, report computed inside the CRM per agency, enforced by separate tenancy, API parity, data boundary and ranking blindness, with an evidence pack for the annual independent review.
